result.why_top_candidate_wins: signal_chile_flu has the strongest combined score (7) and the most direct, relevant edges in the support subgraph: it is a LEADING_INDICATOR_FOR the failed target signal_us_hosp (directly explaining a later US hospital peak) and it also has both IMPORTATION_LINK and POSSIBLE_DRIVER_OF edges into the eq_us_flu_base mechanism. Those two mechanism-level edges create a direct pathway by which Chile activity can increase US importation-driven incidence and hence hospitalizations, matching the observed underprediction (actual_above_prediction, missed_peak). By contrast, Australia (score 5) lacks an explicit IMPORTATION_LINK in the provided evidence (it only has leading-indicator + possible-driver), and Travel Importation Pressure (score 4) lacks the LEADING_INDICATOR_FOR link to the target. Therefore Chile provides both temporal lead information on the target and a mechanistic importation pathway into the model, making it the most plausible single hidden driver given the graph evidence and ranking.
result.proposed_minimal_edit: Add or strengthen an explicit importation forcing term from signal_chile_flu into eq_us_flu_base: create an IMPORTATION_DRIVING_TERM edge (signal_chile_flu -> eq_us_flu_base) and expose a single importation weight parameter to be estimated (e.g., alpha_chile_import). Test re-fitting the model with alpha_chile_import > 0 to see if the missed_peak underprediction for signal_us_hosp is reduced.
result.caveat: This recommendation is based solely on the provided graph edges and scores; it does not prove causality. Temporal validation (checking that Chile peaks consistently lead US hospital peaks) and parameter estimation are required. There may also be confounders (other unobserved regions or travel channels) not represented in the subgraph.
